name: Zigbee (IEEE 802.15.4)
label: Zigbee
notes: Zigbee frames on IEEE 802.15.4, decoded by OnAir's receiver through the onair-rx handler; the row has no decoder of its own, so only a handler runs it. One job reads one channel: start it on a channel's centre with a band of 2 MHz (the handler takes 4 MHz of IQ, OnAir's minimum, and the frequency picks the PHY: O-QPSK at 2.4 GHz, the BPSK PHY below 1 GHz). Each event is a frame whose check sequence passed: `frame_type` (`beacon`, `data`, `ack`, `command`, or OnAir's names for the 2015 types), `seq`, `pan` (4 hex digits), `src` and `dst` (4 hex digits for a short address, 16 for an extended one; null on a frame with none, such as an ack), `nwk_src` and `nwk_dst` (when the Zigbee network header is in the clear) and `secured` (the MAC, NWK or APS layer is secured). Nothing is decrypted and no key is loaded; each PSDU with its FCS (link type 195) goes to a packet capture. Ranges and bands: the sixteen 2.4 GHz channels 11 to 26 (2405 MHz plus 5 MHz a channel, 2 MHz wide) are IEEE 802.15.4's channel page 0, and the sub-GHz ranges (868 to 868.6 MHz, 902 to 928 MHz) are its BPSK PHY's channels 0 to 10; the sub-GHz BPSK PHY has no test signal and is untested, so the row's check proves the 2.4 GHz PHY only. Listing bar: measured on the build host (12 cores) through a scratch node's release build, 30 s of the generated capture looping on a file source and fed in real time; the job skipped no input, onair-rx used 0.58 of a core and the node 0.28 of a core (load average 6.2 to 5.3, with another build running).
